$comment: WHAT: Deterministic enforcement for the rules in AGENTS.md.
WHY:  AGENTS.md is delivered to the model as a user message, not as system config.
The model judges relevance and may skip rules it deems unrelated to the task.
That is by design, not a bug. Anything that must happen 100% of the time
belongs here, at the shell level, where the model has no vote.
Rule of thumb: AGENTS.md is what the agent must KNOW. Hooks are what must
HAPPEN regardless of what it knows.
CONSUMED BY: Claude Code. Codex and Cursor read AGENTS.md but not this file --
the same checks run in CI, so enforcement is identical for every agent.
CONTRACT: hooks receive the event as JSON on stdin. The edited path is
tool_input.file_path. There is no $CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS variable -- an earlier
version of this file used one, so `ruff format $CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS` expanded
to `ruff format` and reformatted the entire tree on every edit. Every hook
below is now a Python script that parses stdin properly and runs on any OS.
PREVENTION vs FEEDBACK: only PreToolUse can stop something -- it runs before the
tool call and exit 2 cancels it. PostToolUse fires after the write has
landed, so it can only tell the agent what it just did. The map below says
which is which. A map that overstates its own power is the thing it exists

hooks.$comment: Denies edits to vendor/ and any write while on main. Golden fixtures escalate to 'ask' rather than deny -- blocking them outright pushes people to disable the hook, and a human in the loop is the actual requirement. Authorised by a one-shot sentinel file the hook deletes after use, not an env var that can be left set in a shell profile.

One script, not three. Formats only the file named in tool_input.file_path, then runs the structural and convention guards and reports failures on the turn that caused them. ADVISORY: the write has already happened by the time this runs. ci:guards is what blocks. Three separate hooks would also have run in parallel rather than in order.

Writes a session record to docs/plans/ naming what changed and whether docs/CODEBASE.md moved with it. Never blocks -- a Stop hook that fails ends the session in an error nobody asked for, and the record is worth less than the interruption costs.

$enforcement_map.$comment: Every rule in AGENTS.md maps to exactly one enforcement mechanism. A rule with no mechanism is advisory and must be tagged as such in AGENTS.md. Machine-checked in both directions by scripts/guard/check_enforcement_map.py: every guard:/ci:/hook: token below must resolve to a real guard file, justfile recipe, workflow job or registered hook event, and every file in scripts/guard/ must be invoked by something.
$enforcement_map.a validation tool consumes the artefact: ADVISORY -- docs/CORRECTIONS.md entry 3; no guard distinguishes a legitimate constructor from a drifting reconstruction
